rows.why: S1 includes zero-valued inputs ('0s' giving 0, '1d0h0m0s0ms' giving 86400000). Item 9 asks whether zero-valued components are accepted, and its pick accepts them and returns the sum. Item 7 (day unit) also fits the 'd' examples, but item 9 is closer to the zero-component cases.
Item 3 asks whether whitespace is tolerated. Its pick trims leading and trailing whitespace, so '  45m\n' parses to 2700000, as S2 expects.

S3 mixes several kinds of bad input, so no single item covers all of it. Item 5 (decimals, signs, ASCII-only digits) covers the most rows: '1.5h', '-3s', '+3s' and the full-width '３s'. Its pick rejects all of these. Other rows map to other items: empty string to 2, '90' to 1, inner spaces to 3, '3S' to 4, '3w' to 7. The '05s' row conflicts with item 9's pick, which accepts leading zeros.
No item asks whether a count may be larger than the next unit up, such as 90m. Item 6 is about order and repeats, not count size.
Item 6 asks about out-of-order and repeated components. Its pick requires units from largest to smallest, each at most once, and errors otherwise, so all four rows are rejected.
Item 8 asks for the largest accepted duration. Its pick caps it at 9007199254740991 ms, so that exact value parses without error.
Item 8 also asks what happens above the cap. Its pick returns 0 and an error, and it checks for overflow while parsing, which covers the 20-digit ms count.

Item 11 asks how FormatDuration splits a value into units, including days. Its pick breaks the value into d/h/m/s/ms and skips zero parts, which gives '1m30s', '1h30m', '1d' and '1d1h1m1s1ms'. Item 10 covers only the zero row, and its pick of '0ms' also agrees.
Item 11's pick uses days and never prints more than 23h, so the maximum value prints as '104249991d8h59m991ms'.
No item asks whether formatting and then parsing returns the original number.

Item 12 asks what FormatDuration does with negative or oversized values. Its pick returns "" and an error for values below 0 or above 9007199254740991, which covers all four rows. The pick does not say what the error message contains.
